topic: How does the 5-minute C/N reporting interval constrain payload resource allocation and network scheduling algorithms?
consensus_response: The 5-minute C/N reporting interval introduces latency in capacity requests and allocations, leading to wasted capacity and potential interference. This constraint affects Load Balancing (LB) and Perceptive Scheduling (PS), which rely on real-time channel condition updates. The timing advance procedure, affected by the 5-minute C/N reporting interval, introduces latency in uplink transmission timing, increasing the risk of interference. Predictive Scheduling can mitigate these effects by forecasting channel conditions, but its effectiveness depends on accurate predictions and timely updates.
